problems.source_text: “When you hear hoof-beats, think of horses not zebras.”
problems.reason: The quoted aphorism drops the word "of" from the source's wording.

problems.location: Concept 4: Reconstructive Memory, Knowledge Integration, and Inferential Reasoning / block 1
problems.lesson_text: Memories are not fixed but instead morph over time... What people report will change over time as new information and suggestions become incorporated into the rich, potentially multisensory tapestry of representations.
problems.source_text: memories are not fixed but instead morph over time, and they may omit details or include fabricated details that did not occur. This is especially evident when people repeatedly remember the same event: what people report will change over time as new information and suggestions become incorporated into the rich, potentially multisensory tapestry of representations physically consolidated across the brain.
problems.reason: The quote ends mid-sentence and silently drops "physically consolidated across the brain", closing it with a period as if the sentence were complete.

problems.location: Concept 3: Sociocultural Foundations and Dynamic Neurobiological Development / block 1
problems.lesson_text: Synapses activated regularly by the learner’s linguistic, social, and physical environment are strengthened and stabilized via myelination, while unused pathways are eliminated.
problems.source_text: the synapses that are continually used during this period are retained, while those that are not used are eliminated ... the dramatic increase in synaptic connections among neurons (gray matter) and in the myelination of nerve fibers (white matter)
problems.reason: Myelination wraps nerve fibers (white matter), not synapses; the source keeps synapse retention and myelination as separate processes, so saying synapses are stabilized via myelination is wrong.

problems.location: Concept 4: Reconstructive Memory, Knowledge Integration, and Inferential Reasoning / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Dual/Disc Earth: Reconciles roundness with perceived flatness by assuming humans live on a flat plate atop a sphere.
problems.source_text: concluding that Earth is shaped like a pancake (or disc): people do not fall off the round (flat) Earth because they live on the top portion of the pancake! ... Five alternative mental models of the Earth were identified: the rectangular Earth, the disc Earth, the dual Earth, the hollow sphere, and the flattened sphere.
problems.reason: In the source's disc model the Earth itself is a flat disc with no sphere, and the dual Earth is a separate model, so the lesson's merged "flat plate atop a sphere" contradicts the source.

problems.location: Concept 4: Reconstructive Memory, Knowledge Integration, and Inferential Reasoning / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Linear Causality: Attributing complex emergent events to a single prominent, visible actor or proximate cause.
problems.source_text: This kind of design-based reasoning is incorporated into problem-based learning (Hmelo-Silver, 2004) activities.
problems.reason: The source cites Hmelo-Silver (2004) only for problem-based learning; the linear-causality misconception, its expert model and its remedy appear in no source.
